receives a pending Promise, the component suspends and React shows the fallback. React doesn't keep any state for a render that suspended before it ever mounted; when the Promise settles, it retries that render from scratch. If the component created the Promise during render, the retry creates a brand-new one, which is pending again, so the component suspends again. React's
docs warn that a Promise created directly in render makes React display the fallback on every re-render, and prevents content from appearing.

The docs' preferred shape is to create the Promise before render, in an event handler, a route loader or a Server Component, and pass it to the component that calls

. Fetching lazily during render delays the request until that component renders and can create waterfalls. A Server Component can even start a request without awaiting it and hand the Promise to a Client Component as a prop: only the part of the page that reads it waits, inside its own boundary, while the rest renders.
